transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I’m just really worn out. I don’t want to make too big a deal of it, but lately even getting from the bedroom to the kitchen feels like I’ve been hauling lumber all day. And resting doesn’t really seem to give me anything back, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to sound dramatic, but yes. I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling in my chest, and it’s hard to shake. Some days I end up just sitting out in the garage and crying, and I can’t even tell you what set it off. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed recently?

Yeah… that’s changed, I guess. I used to really look forward to choir, playing a little pickup ball, working on cars… even grilling for everybody. Now it’s like I know I should want to go, but I just can’t make myself care enough to show up. I’ve even been bad about answering texts from people, which I know isn’t right. Is that what you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess… about four months now. It sort of started after my wife went back to working full-time, and I’ve been home by myself most weekdays. I kept thinking it would pass once I got used to the routine, but it’s… it’s still been there. Does that sound right?
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

I… I don’t want you to think I’m trying to get attention or anything. But yeah, the thought keeps coming up that I should just be dead. And when I’m by myself, it scares me, because I start thinking I might actually do something to make that happen. Is that… okay to say that here?
Have you noticed any changes in how quickly or slowly you're moving compared to how you used to?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if it’s noticeable to other people, but it feels like everything I do is slower. Like my body’s moving through mud or something. Even when someone asks me a question, I hear it, I understand it, but it takes me a while to get the words to come out. I’m not trying to be difficult… it just kind of happens.
Have you lost any weight recently?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed my clothes fitting much differently or anything. I haven’t been keeping track of my weight, though… should I have been?
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I’m not sure I’d call it anxious exactly. I feel uneasy sometimes, like I can’t quite settle, but I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you thought about how you would hurt yourself if you were to act on those thoughts?

I… I don’t want you to think I’m trying to do something right now. But the thought keeps coming up that maybe I should just be dead. And when I’m alone, it scares me, because I start wondering if I might actually do something to make that happen. I’m sorry… is that what you’re asking?
Have you thought about a specific method to hurt yourself?

I don’t… I don’t really have one clear method picked out, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that the thought keeps coming back that I should just be dead, and when I’m alone I get scared because I start thinking I might actually do something to make that happen. I’m sorry, I know that’s not a very good answer.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or that you're looking forward to?

I wish I could say yes. I mean, I used to have things… choir, playing pickup ball, working on cars, grilling when the family was around. Those were things I looked forward to.

Lately, though, I just… I can’t seem to make myself care enough to go. People text me about it and I don’t even answer sometimes. I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything. It’s just like the interest isn’t there.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure most of the day, every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days it’s like I just can’t feel much enjoyment from anything.

I used to really look forward to choir, pickup ball, working on cars, grilling for the family… and now I can’t seem to make myself care enough to show up. Sometimes people text me about it and I don’t even answer. I know that’s not good. It’s just… the pleasure part feels gone most of the time, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and hopelessness are interfering with your ability to function at work or take care of things at home?

Yeah… I mean, I’m not working right now, so I don’t want to overstate it like I’m missing shifts or anything. But at home, yes. I’m not keeping up with the house the way I should.

I had all these handyman plans, little projects I was supposed to do, and I just… don’t follow through. Things sit there, and my wife ends up worrying about everything.

And I guess the part I’m embarrassed to say is she’s scared to leave me alone sometimes, because when the thoughts get really bad, I don’t really trust myself either. I know that’s probably important to tell you.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and hopelessness are present nearly every day?

Yeah… nearly every day, I’d say. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling in my chest most mornings.

Some days I just end up sitting out in the garage and crying, and I can’t even tell you what set it off. It’s embarrassing to admit, but… yeah, it’s there a lot.
Do you feel like these feelings of sadness and hopelessness are worse in the morning or are they pretty consistent throughout the day?

It’s probably worse in the morning, I think. I don’t want to make too much of it, but I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling in my chest, and it kind of sets the tone.

Sometimes it eases a little later, but some days I just end up sitting out in the garage crying and I don’t even really know what started it. I’m sorry… I don’t know if that answers it right.
Do you feel like you're able to find some moments of happiness or relief from your sad feelings, even if they're brief?

Not really… I mean, maybe here and there, but it doesn’t last. I used to look forward to things, you know—choir, playing a little pickup ball, working on cars, grilling for everybody.

Now I just… I can’t seem to make myself care enough to go. People text me and I’ll see it, and I just don’t answer. It sounds bad saying it out loud, but it’s like those things should make me feel better, and they just don’t. Is that what you mean?
Have you experienced any significant weight loss over the past few months?

I don’t think so… not anything significant that I’ve noticed, anyway. My clothes don’t seem, you know, dramatically looser or anything.

I haven’t really been keeping track on a scale, though, so I don’t want to give you the wrong answer. Is that okay?
Do you feel like you're unable to take care of your basic needs, like feeding yourself or bathing, because of these feelings?

I mean… I’m still getting by with the basics most days, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But the house has really gotten away from me, and I keep saying I’m going to fix things or do handyman jobs and then I just… don’t follow through. My wife’s been handling more than she should.

And, um… she’s scared to leave me alone sometimes. Not because I’d do anything on purpose, I don’t want to upset you, but when the thoughts get really bad, I don’t trust myself very much. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Are these feelings of sadness and hopelessness with you for most of the day, or are they more intermittent?

It’s… most of the day, I think. I don’t want to exaggerate, but I wake up with this heavy, hopeless feeling right in my chest, and it kind of follows me around.

Some days I’ll just end up sitting out in the garage and crying, and I don’t even really know what started it. It’s embarrassing to say, but… yeah, it’s not just here and there. Is that what you mean?
